chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: A man gives a thousand dirhams from the zakat, so he distributes it, and he discusses with himself that he should give it to a man from it, then he changes his mind about him and isolates him and gives it to someone else. He said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it
key_terms.يَعْزِلَهُ: He isolates him / sets him aside
key_terms.يُبْدِي لَهُ: He changes his mind / it becomes apparent to him

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to change the intended recipient of zakat after deciding to give it?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility in zakat distribution, affirming that the giver retains the right to alter their intended recipient before the transfer is finalized, a ruling derived from the principle of discretionary preference (tarjih) among the deserving. It underscores the scholarly view that zakat is a right of the giver to allocate among the eight categories mentioned in the Quran, provided the funds are not yet irrevocably assigned. This ruling facilitates efficient distribution by allowing givers to respond to immediate needs or better candidates without invalidating the initial intent.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘

I said to himasws, ‘The man has a thousand Dirhams to give out from the Zakāt. So he distributes it, and he discusses with himself that he should be giving it to the man from it, then he changes his mind about him and he isolates him and gives it to someone else’. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Isma‘il ibn Marrar from Yunus from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about a man who is required to pay Zakat in the amount of one thousand dirham. He distributes it and thinks to give a certain amount to a certain person but then for some reason he gives it to someone else. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
